newsitem.title: USA: Western claims victory in KC Power vote.
newsitem.headline: Western claims victory in KC Power vote.

text.p: Western Resources Inc claimed victory on Thursday after a preliminary vote count showed Kansas City Power and Light Co failed to get majority shareholder approval of its proposed merger with UtiliCorp United Inc.
"There is only one offer on the table now and it is the one that offers $31 per share and a dividend increase up to 45 percent," Western Chairman John Hayes said in a statement.
Western, which has a competing, hostile bid for KC Power, said the vote against the UtiliCorp merger was consistent with its initial vote projections from last month.

"The minority voting in favor of the UtiliCorp proposal, which represents only 38 percent of the shares outstanding, clearly shows that KCPL shareholders recognized the greater value in the Western Resources offer," Hayes said.
Hayes said Western would continue on its course to have KC Power shareholders tender their shares to Western Resources.
On August 30, Western extended the expiration date of its exchange offer to October 25 from September 20.

The official vote count was conducted by the Corporation Trusty Co in Wilmington, Delaware and showed only 46.9 percent of the KC Power shares voting at the August 16 meeting had approved the KC Power/UtiliCorp merger.
